extracted.intended_audience: readers, instructors, and editors of Terence Tao's Analysis I textbook (students and adopters of the book)
extracted.subtask_description: A comprehensive list of errata and editorial corrections for Terence Tao's Analysis I textbook (various editions), indicating required changes to statements, definitions, exercises, proofs, punctuation, references, and pedagogical remarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct cross-references and numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: References to theorems, propositions, corollaries, exercises, and chapters must point to the correct numbered item (e.g., 'Corollary 2.3.7 should be Corollary 4.1.9', 'Lemma 11.8.1 should be Lemma 11.8.4', renumber Analysis II references by lowering chapter numbers by 11).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fix mistaken citation numbers throughout (examples given across many pages). When a chapter renumbering occurs (Analysis II), update all intertext references consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct mathematical mappings and types
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions, mappings, and type declarations must state the correct domain and codomain (e.g., 'f should map Z to W, and h should map X to Y', 'is a function from X to Z' corrections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all function declarations and usages explicitly mention correct source/target sets in statements and proofs; fix swapped or incorrect mappings in lemmas and their proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include all necessary hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements, definitions, lemmas, propositions, and exercises must include any missing hypotheses required for the result to hold (examples: add hypothesis that A is non-empty; add n>0 in Proposition 4.3.10(b); add x non-zero in Exercise 5.6.3; require limit points in Lemma 10.4.1 and Theorem 10.4.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audit each result for implicit assumptions; explicitly add them when omitted (the errata lists many specific instances).

rubrics_metrics.name: State when axiom of choice (or other axioms) is required
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly note when an exercise, lemma, or proposition depends on the axiom of choice or specific axioms from the text (e.g., 'This exercise requires the axiom of choice from Section 8.4', 'Lemma 8.2.5 requires the axiom of choice').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag dependence on non-constructive axioms in the statement or a note; similarly indicate when well-ordering principle or least upper bound is needed for existence/uniqueness claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use precise logical language ('if' vs 'iff')
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace casual or ambiguous logical phrasing with precise logical connectors where appropriate (e.g., 'if' should be 'iff' in definitions and equivalences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check definitions and statements of equivalence and replace 'if' with 'iff' when biconditional is intended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent and standard terminology (codomain vs range, conditional convergence phrasing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer standard/consistent terminology across the book (e.g., change all occurrences of 'range' to 'codomain'; replace 'conditionally divergent' with 'not conditionally convergent' and 'absolutely divergent' with 'not absolutely convergent').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use canonical terms for clarity and to match standard texts; update index and all occurrences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct spelling, grammar, and punctuation
rubrics_metrics.description: Fix typographical, spelling, and grammatical errors (e.g., 'solidifed' -> 'solidified', 'to to' -> 'to', capitalization 'can you add' -> 'Can you add', punctuation inside parentheses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply consistent English punctuation rules (periods inside parentheses where appropriate), correct capitalization at sentence starts, and correct misspellings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper typesetting and math-mode usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure mathematical content is set in math mode and formatting is correct (e.g., 'On the final line, should be in math mode', 'replace occurrences with proper math-mode formatting').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check inline and display math, spacing issues, and ensure symbols are typeset rather than plain text where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct displays and algebraic/formula corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace incorrect displayed equations or sums with the intended expressions wherever displays are wrong (numerous display-by-display corrections listed, e.g., replace one sum by another, fix limit sets, fix missing ellipses, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify each display against surrounding context and correct the formulas; ensure indices and summations are correct in proofs and exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add missing punctuation to displays and sentences
rubrics_metrics.description: Insert missing periods, commas, parentheses, or ellipses at the ends of displays or sentences (e.g., 'a period is missing at the end of ...', 'ellipsis is missing in final display').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure each sentence and displayed equation ends with correct punctuation where prose requires it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify definitions by adding phrases or examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Add clarifying sentences or remarks to definitions to avoid ambiguity (e.g., 'In Definition 4.3.9, after “...” add “; in particular, we define ...”, add 'let ... be a real number' to Definition 9.10.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a definition omits an instantiation or special-case convention, explicitly add it to prevent misinterpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fix incorrect or misleading hints in exercises
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove or correct misleading hints that require results not covered (e.g., 'the hint is misleading (it requires the mean value theorem for integrals rather than for derivatives) and should be deleted').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure hints reference only material available prior to the exercise or clearly state dependencies; delete hints that imply unavailable prerequisites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure exercises are placed where prerequisites exist
rubrics_metrics.description: Move or reorder exercises to sections where their prerequisites have been introduced (e.g., 'Exercise 11.25.10 should be Exercise 4.25.10 of Analysis II', 'move Exercise 11.4.2 to Section 11.5 since it uses Corollary 11.5.2').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reorganize exercises so that readers have the necessary background before attempting them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add or modify exercises and hints where needed
rubrics_metrics.description: Add missing exercises, split exercises into parts, or add recommended hints (e.g., add Exercise 5.5.5, split Exercise 3.5.1 into three parts, add hints like '(Hint: use Exercise 5.2.2.)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide constructive guidance or additional optional exercises to fill pedagogical gaps noted in the errata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make uniqueness/existence statements precise
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace vague existential claims with precise uniqueness/existence formulations (e.g., 'Then there is a unique set of the form … . That is to say, there is a set ... such that for any ... iff ...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where proofs rely on uniqueness, restate the result in the exact logical form required for the argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require non-emptiness when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Add 'non-empty' hypotheses where needed for definitions, exercises, or lemmas (e.g., endpoints of intervals defined only when interval is non-empty; add 'non-empty' before 'totally ordered subset').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audit uses of inf/sup, endpoints, minima, and similar concepts and require non-emptiness explicitly when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify domain/codomain and image before use
rubrics_metrics.description: Define the image and codomain of functions prior to using these notions in subsequent sections or remarks (e.g., 'image is not defined until that section', 'we extend these notions to functions that take values in a subset by identifying such functions ...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order definitions so that dependent terminology is introduced only after its prerequisites; add clarifying paragraphs where order was previously reversed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify conventions about identification/abuse of notation
rubrics_metrics.description: When the text implicitly identifies objects of different types (e.g., natural numbers with their counterparts in integers), make an explicit remark about this abuse of notation and its safe use, and add conventions (e.g., add paragraph about identifying objects of one type with another).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add explanatory remarks to warn readers when identification is being used and under what circumstances it is safe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct historical or factual asides
rubrics_metrics.description: Fix incorrect biographical or factual notes (e.g., 'Paul Cohen (1934-)' -> 'Paul Cohen (1934-2007)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure any historical asides or dates are accurate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replace ambiguous phrases with standard mathematical phrasing
rubrics_metrics.description: Change casual or ambiguous wording to standard precise phrasing (e.g., 'unique object ...' -> 'unique object ...', 'laws of equality' -> 'axioms of equality').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer standard textbook phrasing to reduce reader confusion and align with established conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add missing parenthetical remarks and clarifications in proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Insert omitted parenthetical remarks or clarifying clauses that are needed to make a proof complete or understandable (e.g., add '(omitting the ... condition when ...)', add comments about temporarily defining an expression 'for the purposes of this lemma').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a proof invokes an extension or temporary definition, explicitly state this and justify why it is acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure index and cross-references reflect corrected terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Update index and cross-references to reflect terminology changes (e.g., change index entries when 'range' replaced by 'codomain').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform global updates to index, table of contents, and references when terminology is altered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify conventions for degenerate or edge cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Add conventions or special-case instructions for degenerate situations (e.g., define series on finite sets to be automatically absolutely convergent; convention for empty or singleton intervals in Definition 11.8.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state conventions used for boundary cases to avoid ambiguity in statements and proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct sequence/indexing conventions in examples and exercises
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure sequences and sums start at the intended index (e.g., sequences should start from n=1 rather than 0, limits over correct index sets, 'all sequences here should start from 1 rather than from 0').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniformly adopt and correct indexing conventions in examples and exercises; note and correct where sequence start indices were inconsistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fix proof steps that rely on incorrect references or equalities
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace incorrect appeals or equalities in proofs with correct lemmas or corrected algebra (e.g., 'Replace “from Corollary 6.1.17” here by “from Lemma 5.1.15 ...”', 'the first inequality should be an equality').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify each step of proofs and ensure referenced results actually imply the needed claim; correct algebraic manipulations and references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add missing exercises or notes to justify existence/uniqueness arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: When an exercise or proof glosses over existence/uniqueness, add a note or exercise pointing to the justifying principle (e.g., add note that to ensure existence/uniqueness of a minimum one needs well-ordering principle or least upper bound principle).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure core existence/uniqueness claims are supported by explicit references to theorems or axioms, or add new exercises to demonstrate them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be explicit when changing convention across editions
rubrics_metrics.description: When edition differences (paperback vs hardback) affect page numbering or references, explicitly warn readers how to apply errata across editions (e.g., 'first edition paperback page numbers differ from the second (or third) edition hardback page numbers').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide mapping notes or instructions so readers of different editions can apply the errata correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct minor layout/spacing issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Fix missing spaces, misplaced parentheses, and spacing errors in the prose and formulas (e.g., 'a space missing between “the” and “Zermelo”', 'add a space before (why?)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small layout fixes should be applied throughout to improve readability and avoid misreading formulas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure definitions align with standard mathematical objects (e.g., ordered tuples, products)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where constructions might be incompatible or ambiguous (e.g., two different constructions of ordered tuples), either reconcile them or remark on the harmless incompatibility and provide guidance (e.g., split exercises and add remark about compatibility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple constructions exist, note compatibility issues and either choose one convention or explain how to translate between them.
